questions.cardText:
[History] What is the origin of the term “knot” as a measure of speed?
A. It was named after a famous sailor
B. It originated from a method using knotted ropes
C. It was a topological reference
Answer: B. The term “knot” comes from an old maritime practice where sailors used a “log line” with knots tied at regular intervals. The number of knots that passed through the sailor’s hands in a specific time period indicated the ship’s speed in nautical miles per hour.
questions.de: Die Geschwindigkeitseinheit „Knoten“ stammt von einem alten Gerät der Seeleute: einem Holzbrett an einer Leine mit Knoten in regelmäßigen Abständen, die während einer festen Zeit beim Ablaufen gezählt wurden. Wie hieß dieses Gerät?
questions.en: The unit of speed “knot” comes from an old sailors’ device: a wooden float on a line knotted at regular intervals, whose knots were counted as they ran out over a set time. What was this device called?

timeline.labelEn: William Bourne's “A Regiment for the Sea” gives the first known printed description of the chip log
timeline.labelDe: William Bournes „A Regiment for the Sea“ beschreibt als erstes bekanntes Druckwerk die Relingslogge

questions.notes: Answer cross-checked on Wikipedia: Knot (unit) — knots tied 47 ft 3 in apart, timed with a sand-glass. German name: Logge / Handlogge.

questions.cardText:
[Linguistics] What is a “morpheme”?
A. The smallest meaningful unit in language
B. A language family in North Africa
C. A long poem
Answer: A.“Cat”, “-ness”, “re-“, and “-th” are examples of morphemes, whereas “catness”, “wug”, “mañana”, “f” are not.
questions.de: Wie nennt die Sprachwissenschaft die kleinste bedeutungstragende Einheit der Sprache, etwa „cat“, „-ness“ oder „re-“?
questions.en: What do linguists call the smallest meaningful unit of language, such as “cat”, “-ness” or “re-”?

timeline.labelEn: Jan Baudouin de Courtenay defines the morpheme as the smallest autonomous, indivisible part of a word
timeline.labelDe: Jan Baudouin de Courtenay definiert das Morphem als kleinsten eigenständigen, unteilbaren Teil eines Wortes

questions.notes: Coinage date of the term disputed (1895/1896; concept from early 1880s), hence approx. The card's example list ("catness", "wug", "mañana" not morphemes) is odd but irrelevant to the open question.
